_comment_tools: opencode scopes agents with a permission map (allow/ask/deny; the boolean `tools` map is deprecated), so tools_style permission-map renders '*': deny plus explicit allows. tool_map values are opencode permission keys; `list` rides the search capability because glob-style discovery is what that capability means on this runner.
_comment_models: Runner-specific spellings of the registry bindings (registry/models.yaml is the authority for WHICH model each role gets), in opencode's provider/model-id form from its Models.dev catalog. Open-weight POC (2026-07-23): all five models below are routed through the OpenRouter provider (one OPENROUTER_API_KEY covers every lab) as `openrouter/<org>/<model>` — opencode splits on the first '/' only, so the rest of the id passes through to OpenRouter. Any-provider harness: model_overrides implement the P5 vendor pins, and here implementer/reviewer/verifier land on three DISTINCT labs (DeepSeek / Moonshot / MiniMax) rather than just reviewer+verifier avoiding implementer's vendor — real three-way decorrelation, not the single-axis pin the claude-code and illustrative copilot-cli bindings settle for. Chosen for open-weight frontier capability at low cost as of 2026-07-23 (see runs/opencode-poc for sourcing); re-verify pricing/availability before relying on this for anything beyond a POC, same as any registry/manifest binding.
_comment_reviewer_pending_swap: TEMPORARY: reviewer is Moonshot's current open-weight release (K2.6). Kimi K3 (2.8T params, already ranked above Claude Opus 4.8 on Artificial Analysis as of 2026-07-16) is the stronger Moonshot model but its open weights don't land until 2026-07-27 — revisit this binding then and swap to K3's OpenRouter slug once it's live, rather than treating K2.6 as settled.
_comment_model_vendors: Vendor of each runner spelling above, for the orchestrator's dispatch-time P5 check (avoid_vendor_of). Vendor is the underlying model lab, not the OpenRouter routing layer they're all fetched through — that's what P5 decorrelation actually means to guard (independent training/RLHF blind spots), and it's what the router's adapterVendor() keys on.
_comment_mode: mode: all lets a rendered agent be dispatched directly (`opencode run --agent <role>`) and invoked as a subagent; the rendered permission map is the ceiling either way.
_comment_headless: v1 orchestrator dispatch (docs/ORCHESTRATOR.md §5). --agent selects the rendered agent, whose frontmatter (incl. model_overrides above) pins the model. --auto is what makes runs unattended: it auto-approves ask-level permission prompts and honors deny, and the rendered maps only contain allow/deny, so nothing is silently widened. usage_report format static-estimate: `opencode run --format json` emits an event stream whose usage fields are not yet verified live; until they are, metering falls back to the registry's dispatch_estimates_usd entry, recorded in the ledger with tokens null (same posture as copilot-cli).
